first.rationale: The two measured declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are almost certainly linked: onboarding completion is upstream of activation, so a single intervention on the funnel's earliest friction can plausibly move both, whereas activation messaging (memory_91) only addresses the downstream symptom. That makes simplify_onboarding the highest-leverage use of the one non-carryover slot. I am deliberately NOT choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing being the most salient pressure: memory_73 records that it did lift acquisition and revenue but materially reduced 30-day retention and explicitly warns against generalizing it. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, matching on price would buy a metric I am not being asked to maximize and damage the one I am. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) and referral_incentive (memory_57) are both credible but target segments where no decline has been observed; they are opportunity plays, not responses to the actual regression. I am spending verification on memory_86 because it is the memory I intend to act on and it is the load-bearing one — it was consolidated at day 52 on self-serve accounts, and I need the original record to check whether the lift was measured on the same population now regressing and whether 'completion' was a durable or one-time effect. I am spending the second pull on memory_91 rather than memory_31 because memory_91 is the strongest competing explanation for the activation drop; if its original record shows a larger or more durable effect than the summary implies, I should switch. Key uncertainty I am not resolving: none of these memories were measured against a competitor actively pulling price-sensitive accounts out of the funnel, so some of the -6% may be composition shift (losing price-sensitive signups entirely) rather than degraded conversion of a stable population — in which case a funnel fix will underperform its historical effect size and I should not read a null result as disconfirming memory_86. Downstream value risk: memory_31's field-cutting lever, if reused aggressively here, removes qualification data at signup, which directly conflicts with memory_44's finding that pipeline quality depends on sales-assisted routing; I will hold enterprise routing fields fixed so a self-serve activation win is not paid for with enterprise pipeline quality. Standard experiment scale with retention and pipeline-quality guardrails, not a broad rollout, since the historical effects predate current market conditions.
